Method of Attack: Collects files, passwords, cookies, browser history, cryptocurrency wallets, banking credentials
Acts as downloader for other malware families in multi-stage campaigns
Steals cryptocurrency from locally available wallets (Electrum, Bitcoin, Etherium, etc.)
Steals FTP logins and passwords from FileZilla
Steals information from locally installed browsers including cookies
Steals credentials for WinSCP, Pidgin messenger and others
Exfiltrates collected data to command-and-control server
Impacted Systems: Windows systems infected by fake ProtonVPN installer
Systems with locally installed cryptocurrency wallets (Electrum, Bitcoin, Etherium)
Systems with FileZilla, WinSCP, Pidgin messenger
Attack Vector: Fake ProtonVPN website (protonvpn.store) delivering fake ProtonVPN installers
Downloading and executing fake ProtonVPN installer named ProtonVPN_win_v1.10.0.exe
